house:119:1:199.question: On Passage
house:119:1:199.reason: Checkpoint 191 fully reads the complete 252-page July print and the 133,704-character Senate GENIUS text and confirms own July 17 passage identity. Existing Health shared core/ref/digests remain unchanged. No Immigration clearance, component member stance, new meaning/proposition, acceptance or enacted/current-law claim. H.R. 3633 is Rules Committee Print 119-6 read with adopted Report 119-199 Part B and floor sections 106(c), 405(a)-(b), and 409 operators; unoffered Sherman Part C and later September Title VI are excluded. Financial registration, custody, insolvency, foreign-supervision and AML/customer-ID rules retain their scope. New GENIUS section 22 says United States individual for qualified personal self-custody/peer transactions, not automatically citizen, resident, lawful status or everybody; sanctions/enforcement savings remain. Expedited hiring retains referenced civil-service rules. Keep unresolved/noncounting pending materially affected incorporation and individual-access/status application; no automatic domain fit/exclusion. Own question precedes voice ayes, Craig demand/order and postponement, followed later by recorded passage, 294-134 with four Not Voting; Foushee Nay and Massie Not Voting.

house:119:1:349.question: On Passage
house:119:1:349.reason: The complete 104,445-character H.R. 6703 EH and own declaration/recorded passage are read. Section 103 permits designation of an employee class requiring nonresident-alien tax status AND no earned income from that employer constituting US-source income, within the arrangement's same-terms, coverage, substantiation and notice conditions. This is an optional conjunctive employee class, not all noncitizens, unlawful presence, work authorization, mandatory denial or observed employer action. The original 2019 complete HRA class rule already names a comparable non-resident/no-US-based-income class and retains its class-size/combination/new-hire/student structure. Its reference to 1.105-11(c)(2)(iii)(E) is not silently replaced with the bill's911(d)(2); no first-ever permission or identical legal application is claimed. Existing HR1 HRA scope review reserves this tax/employee-class mechanism for bounded domain review rather than inferring Immigration fit from nonresident wording. The bill's no-inference rule is qualified by consistency with its amendments and requires conforming rules. Current/full integration, tax-definition, Medicare/exchange and cost-sharing beneficiary baselines and exact upstream shared-core adequacy for any domain proposition remain qualified. Keep the action unresolved/noncounting pending the existing bounded domain application and material baseline/source-chain review; do not automatically exclude or include. Association-plan, stop-loss, pharmacy reporting and cost-sharing funding operators remain part of one package. Existing Health core/ref/digests are unchanged. Own passage question precedes voice ayes and Latta demand/order; recorded 216–211 with 6 Not Voting, Foushee Nay and Massie Nay. No new Immigration proposition, interpretation of the shared core, component stance, first-ever status eligibility change, enactment, current implementation or acceptance.
